word_order: SVO | Clauses in the sample consistently place an overt subject before the verb and the object (e.g. 'The capsule will look...', 'Israel demands an ongoing military presence...').
clause_boundary_signals: coordinating conjunctions joining independent clauses (and, but)
subordinating conjunctions introducing subordinate clauses (although, if)
relative pronouns introducing relative clauses (who, that)
sentence-level adverbials that often introduce a new clause (while, because)
non_boundary_traps: initial temporal/locative prepositional phrases that are adjuncts, not main clauses (for over a thousand years, around 60 cases)
participial/gerundial modifiers attached to a verb or noun (causing..., leaving..., going across...)
appositive or parenthetical inserts inside noun phrases (live on television)
prepositional complements inside NPs that look clause-like (of the Apollo X command module)
unstable_prefix_signals: quantifying/adverbial modifiers whose scope can be revised by following material (around 60, only)
subordinating conjunctions or initial adverbials after which the intended attachment/scope may be overturned by continuation (although, while)
negation/contrast markers that may change scope with later material (not, aren't)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Source sentences are formal English with many complex, multi-clause sentences built by subordinators and relative clauses. Adverbial prepositional phrases and participial phrases frequently appear before or inside clauses and do not by themselves mark clause completion. Focus/quantifier words (only, around) and negation can change the meaning of preceding material depending on what follows, so their scope is provisional until the clause continues.
